spotify_data = read.csv("high_popularity_spotify_data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
head(spotify_data)
```

```

```{r}
colSums(is.na(spotify_data))
```
Veiem que hi ha un NA en el track_album_name. El treurem i eliminarem aquelles columnes que considerem que no són importants en el nostre context per realitzar un multivariate analysis.
```{r}
spotify_data_clean <- spotify_data[!is.na(spotify_data$track_album_name), ]
cols_to_remove <- c("track_id", "track_href", "uri", "analysis_url", "id", 
                    "playlist_id", "type", "track_album_id", "key", "mode","time_signature")

spotify_data_clean <- spotify_data_clean[ , !(names(spotify_data_clean) %in% cols_to_remove)]
# Convertir variables enteras a numéricas si es necesario
spotify_data_clean$track_popularity <- as.numeric(spotify_data_clean$track_popularity)
spotify_data_clean$duration_ms <- as.numeric(spotify_data_clean$duration_ms)
names(spotify_data_clean)
```
```{r}
sapply(spotify_data_clean, class)
```
```{r}
library(aplpack)
numeric_data <- spotify_data_clean[ , sapply(spotify_data_clean, is.numeric)]
faces()
faces(numeric_data[1:9,],face.type=0)
faces(numeric_data[1:9,],face.type=1)
```
```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Get the top 5 most frequent genres
top_5_genres <- spotify_data_clean %>%
  count(playlist_genre, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice(1:5) %>%
  pull(playlist_genre)

# Create a new dataset with only the top 5 genres
filtered_data <- spotify_data_clean %>%
  filter(playlist_genre %in% top_5_genres)
# Step 2: Get the top 5 most frequent subgenres within filtered_data
top_5_subgenres <- filtered_data %>%
  count(playlist_subgenre, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice(1:5) %>%
  pull(playlist_subgenre)

# Step 3: Filter again to keep only rows with those top 5 subgenres
sp_filtered <- filtered_data %>%
  filter(playlist_subgenre %in% top_5_subgenres)
```

## LDA

```{r}
# Select numerical columns only
numeric_cols <- sapply(sp_filtered, is.numeric)
sp_numeric <- sp_filtered[, numeric_cols]

## Checking histogram, qqplots and shapiro Willk's test results
for (col_name in colnames(sp_numeric)) {
  cat(col_name)
  print(shapiro.test(sp_numeric[[col_name]]))
  print(ks.test(sp_numeric[[col_name]], "pnorm", mean=mean(sp_numeric[[col_name]]), sd=sd(sp_numeric[[col_name]])))
  qqnorm(sp_numeric[[col_name]], main = col_name)
  hist(sp_numeric[[col_name]], main = col_name)
}
```
```{r}
x11(width = 12, height = 8)  # You can adjust width/height as needed

# Set up grid layout for plots
n_cols <- 3  # Number of columns in the panel
n_rows <- ceiling(length(colnames(sp_numeric)) / n_cols)

par(mfrow = c(n_rows, n_cols), mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2) + 0.1)

# Create boxplots for each numeric variable
for (col_name in colnames(sp_numeric)) {
  boxplot(sp_numeric[[col_name]] ~ sp_filtered$playlist_genre,
          main = paste("Boxplot de", col_name, "por playlist_genre"),
          xlab = "playlist_genre",
          ylab = col_name,
          las = 2,              # Rotate labels for better fit
          col = "lightblue",
          border = "gray40")
}

# Reset layout (optional)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
locator(1)
```
```{r}
# Eliminar variables negatives o amb zeros
sp_input <- sp_numeric[, !(names(sp_numeric) %in% c("instrumentalness", "loudness"))] 

sp_boxcox <- sp_input

# Box Cox transformation
for (var in names(sp_input)) {
  y <- sp_input[[var]]
  bc <- boxcox(lm(y ~ 1), lambda = seq(-2, 2, 0.1))
  lambda_opt <- bc$x[which.max(bc$y)]

  # Apply transformation using the best lambda
  if (lambda_opt == 0) {
    sp_boxcox[[var]] <- log(y)
  } else {
    sp_boxcox[[var]] <- (y^lambda_opt - 1) / lambda_opt
  }
} 

# Standarize
sp_boxcox_scaled <- as.data.frame(scale(sp_boxcox))
```
```{r}
## Checking histogram, qqplots and shapiro Willk's test results
for (col_name in colnames(sp_boxcox_scaled)) {
  cat(col_name)
  print(shapiro.test(sp_boxcox_scaled[[col_name]]))
  print(ks.test(sp_boxcox_scaled[[col_name]], "pnorm", mean=mean(sp_boxcox_scaled[[col_name]]), sd=sd(sp_boxcox_scaled[[col_name]])))
  qqnorm(sp_boxcox_scaled[[col_name]], main = col_name)
  hist(sp_boxcox_scaled[[col_name]], main = col_name)
}
```
```{r}
sp_fit  <- cbind(sp_boxcox_scaled, playlist_genre = as.factor(sp_filtered$playlist_genre))

summary(sp_fit)
str(sp_fit)
```
```{r}
qda.fit <- qda(playlist_genre ~ ., data = sp_fit)
qda.fit
```
```{r}
qda.class <- predict (qda.fit)

tabqda<-table(qda.class$class,sp_fit$playlist_genre)
tabqda
sum(diag(tabqda))/sum(tabqda)
```
```{r}
library(klaR)

pdf("qda_partimat.pdf", width = 14, height = 14)
partimat(playlist_genre ~ ., data = sp_fit, method = "qda")
dev.off()
```

```{r}
### Q statistic
# Q=(n-ñk)^2/n(k-1)
## compared with chi^2 value of (1,0.05)
ny <- sum(diag(tabqda))
n <- nrow(sp_fit)
k <- 5

Qsp <- ((n - ny * k)^2) / (n * (k - 1))
cat("Q statistic:", Qsp, "\n")

q_critical <- qchisq(0.95, df = k - 1)
cat("Critical value (chi-squared, 0.95, df =", k - 1, "):", q_critical, "\n")
```
```{r}
set.seed(2)
# Stepwise Classification
sp_step<-stepclass(sp_boxcox_scaled,sp_fit$playlist_genre,method="qda",direction="backward", criterion="CR", start.vars = c("danceability", "speechiness", "acousticness","duration_ms","track_popularity","valence"))
sp_step

summary(sp_step)
sp_step$process
sp_step$model
sp_step$result.pm

```
```{r}
library(e1071)

sp_naive.fit<-naiveBayes(playlist_genre ~ ., data = sp_fit)
sp_naive.fit
```
```{r}
sp_naive.class <- predict (sp_naive.fit , sp_fit)
table(sp_naive.class, sp_fit$playlist_genre)

mean(sp_naive.class==sp_fit$playlist_genre)
```
```{r}
sp_naive.preds<-predict(sp_naive.fit, sp_fit, type="raw")
sp_naive.preds[1:20,]
```
## MANOVA

```{r}
dependent_vars <- paste(colnames(sp_numeric), collapse = ", ")
formula_str <- paste("cbind(", dependent_vars, ") ~ playlist_genre")


sp_manova <- manova(as.formula(formula_str), data = sp_filtered)
summary.aov(sp_manova)
```
